case_source: (From the judgement and order dated 25th of April, 2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011)
full_judgment:
Md Imman Ali J: This civil appeal, by leave, is directed against the judgement and order dated 25-4-2012 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011 disposing of the rule Nisi.

2. The facts of the case, in short, are that a project namely "Development of Selected Colleges (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised)" (hereinafter "the Project") under the Ministry of Education was started in 1997 which was primarily targeted to be, completed in June, 2005. In the said project a total of 115 hostels were established, and to run the hostels, total 460 posts were created of which 115 posts for Head Cook, 115 for Assistant Cook, 115 for Night Guards and 115 posts for Sweeper. For appointment in those posts an employment notification was published in different newspapers. The present petitioners (who are 129 in number) and others filed applications. Accordingly examination was held for selection of suitable candidates. The writ-petitioners participated in the said examination and were selected. Their names were published in the daily newspapers. Getting appointment letters they joined in their respective posts in different districts. Writ-petitioner Nos. 1-36 joined as Head Cook, Writ-petitioner Nos. 37-68 joined as Assistant Cook, writ-petitioner Nos. 69-97 joined as Sweeper and writ-petitioner Nos. 98-129 joined as Night Guard. After expiry of the project period in June, 2005, the same was extended from time to time till June, 2008. The writ-petitioners and others got salary up to June, 2007. Though it was mentioned that the period of the project would expire in June, 2005, but there was a stipulation in the project proforma that after completion of the project those posts would be transferred to the revenue budget as per Government rules. Several letters were exchanged between the Ministries for taking step to transfer or absorb the service of the writ-petitioners in the revenue budget, but finally the same has not been done, although the writ-petitioners legitimately expected that their service might be transferred/ absorbed in the revenue budget. But the writ-respondents did not take any positive step to transfer/absorb the services of the writ-petitioners in the revenue budget. In such a situation the writ-petitioners issued notice demanding justice, but to no effect. Thereafter, the writ-petitioners moved the High Court Division and obtained the rule Nisi.

3. Writ-respondent Nos. 2 and 3 entered their appearance and contested the Rule by filing two sets of affidavits-in-opposition contending, inter alia, that the provisions made in the project proforma did not give any guarantee to transfer any post and manpower from development project to revenue setup. Transfers of posts from development budget to revenue setup are guided by specific rules and regulations. The Ministry of Establishment did not recommend 460 posts for transfer to the revenue setup. The decision of ECNEC was to transfer the post from project to revenue budget, but the incumbents were not recommended by the Ministry of Establishment because they did not satisfy the necessary rules and regulations. While recruiting the writ-petitioners it was made clear that their appointments would stand terminated at the end of the project. The appointees could not have any legitimate expectation that they would be included in the revenue budget. In such view of the matter the rule Nisi should be discharged.

4. By the impugned judgment and order, the High Court Division disposed of the Rule directing the respondents to consider the case of the writ-petitioners in the light of the decision of ECNEC dated 30-12-2007 and the provisions of SRO No. 182-Ain/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 20-6-2005. Hence, the writ respondents as petitioners filed Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 464 of 2013 and leave was grafted to consider the following submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney-General for the petitioners.

"I. That the project in which the writ petitioners were working was started after 30th June, 1987, and, therefore, the SRO No. 182 dated 20th June, 2005 has no manner of application for the regularisation of the petitioners in the revenue set up and thus, the High Court Division erred in law in directing the petitioners to consider their cases in the light of the said Rules.

II. That since the writ petitioners' project was started after 30th June, 1987, their case is covered by SRO No. 183- Ain/ 2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 20th June, 2005, under which SRO, the writ petitioners cannot claim any right of absorption in the revenue setup. III. That in the absence of proper pleadings laying foundation in support of the claim of legitimate expectation, the High Court Division erred in law in holding that in view of the letter mentioned above, the writ petitioners can claim for regularisation on the doctrine of legitimate expectation."

5. Mr Ekramul Haque, learned Deputy Attorney General appearing on behalf of the appellants made submissions in line with the grounds upon which leave was granted. He further submitted that the High Court Division failed to appreciate that the SRO No. 182-Ain/2005/ Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 dated 29-6-2005 is not applicable for the writ-petitioners, SRO No. 183 Am/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-1/S-9/2000 is applicable for them, but nowhere in SRO No. 183 or in the project proforma or in the appointment letters of the writ-petitioners, is there any express clear promise made that after completion of the project their service would be transferred to the revenue budget, as such, no legitimate expectation arises in respect of the petitioners for absorbing them in the revenue budget, hence, the High Court Division erred in law in making the direction and, as such, the appeal may kindly be allowed. He further submitted that the writ petitioners having not been assured or promised by any authority of the Government that their services would be regularised in the revenue budget after the expiry of the period of the project, the High Court Division erred in law in making the direction as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside and the appeal may kindly be allowed. He further submitted that the writ-petitioners being amenable to the jurisdiction of Administrative Tribunal, writ petition at their behest is not maintainable, hence, the High Court Division erred in law in entertaining the writ petition and making the direction sitting in special statutory jurisdiction under Article 102 of the Constitution of People's Republic of Bangladesh, as such the impugned judgment is liable to be set aside and the appeal may kindly be allowed.

6. Mr Masud Hossain Dolan, learned Advocate appearing for the respondent submitted that the Appellate Division has given eleven guidelines for absorption in the Revenue-setup in several other cases and the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 4013 of 2012 directed the authority concerned to absorb 76 (seventy six) writ petitioners from the "Development of Selected College (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised) to revenue setup in accordance with the Appellate Division's guidelines and after scrutiny of the documents absorbed 66 (sixty-six) employees out of 76 (seventy-six) and still 394 (three hundred ninety four) employees posts are vacant and the writ-petitioners-respondents are still in service and have requisite qualifications, experience and satisfactory service record; and in the similar position the writ-petitioners are expecting to be transferred in the revenue set up and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that the High Court Division correctly held that from the employment notice, Project Proforma and the letters of the Ministry of Education and the Director General of Secondary and Education Directorate, it appears that the respondents while making employment notification assured the writ-petitioners that their services might be transferred /absorbed in the revenue budget. From the letters of the Education Directorate, it appears that even the Government did not depart from the intention to transfer/absorb the services of the petitioners in the revenue budget, rather they failed to take any decision for want of time to make necessary amendment in the organogram of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Directorate; and the petitioners have also been assured through the Principals of the respective colleges wherein the Petitioners had been serving that they would be informed if any positive step is taken to transfer/absorb their services in the revenue budget, and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that the High Court Division correctly held that it is found from the several letters that decision was taken in several meetings that the writ-petitioners-respondents would be absorbed in the revenue set up and the Government is duty bound to absorb the writ-petitioners-respondents by giving assurance, and such an assurance has created a legitimate expectation in the mind of the writ-petitioners-respondent. At this stage, the writ-respondents -appellants now cannot back out from such an assurance and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that after completion of the project work the writ-petitioners-respondents were permitted to continue to work and they were under expectation that they will be absorbed in the revenue set up and the posts of the respondents are required by the Government thus the Ministry of Education recommended to transfer the service of the respondents to the revenue set up and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He also submitted that the petitioners are working in the "Development of Selected Colleges (Government and Non-Government) Project (2nd Revised)" under the Ministry of Education and have not yet been absorbed/regularised in the service of the Republic as such the Administrative Tribunal Act is not attracted/applicable in the present case and the writ-petitioners-respondents have no other equal efficacious remedy and, as such, the Writ Petition No. 3562 of 2011 is maintainable. He submitted that the services of the respondents were legally utilised by appellant Nos. I and 2 for such a long time without any break, but their absorption in the revenue set up was kept hanging without any reason and most illegally and arbitrarily by misusing the position and such the same is without any lawful authority and is of no legal effect and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He submitted that 394 (three hundred ninety four) vacant posts existing in the Ministry of Education have been declared to be filled by direct appointment, which is unfair and discriminatory. The Ministry of Education has on a previous occasion approved the absorption of 66 (sixty six) persons in the vacant posts and if the writ petitioners apply for the direct appointment they would be at a disadvantage due to the fact that they would be over the age limit and the writ-petitioners-respondents have necessary experience and qualification to be transferred in the revenue set up and the same is conventional and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed. He lastly submitted that the Government is duty bound in accordance with the SRO No. 182/ LAW/ 2005/SHOM/BIBIDN/5-9 dated 20-6-2005 and, as such, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.

7. We have considered the submissions of the learned Deputy Attorney General and learned Advocate for the respondents, perused the impugned judgment and order of the High Court Division and other connected papers on record.

8. The High Court Division considered the employment notice, project proforma and the letter dated 30-1-2006 issued by the Ministry of Establishment addressing the Secretary, Ministry of Education and the letter dated 15-2-2006 issued by the Ministry of Education to the Project Director and the Director-General, Secondary and Higher Secondary Education and the letter dated 30.12.2007 issued by the Director-General of the Secondary and Higher Secondary Education Directorate to the Principals of Colleges where the petitioners had been serving and noted that the petitioners' expectation to get their services transferred/absorbed in the revenue setup has got basis. It was also noted that a direction was given by the High Court Division to absorb/regularise the writ-petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5667 of 2008 in almost identical circumstances. The civil petition for leave to appeal filed by the respondents earlier having been dismissed by this Division, the direction of the High Court Division was implemented. Hence, the High Court Division directed the respondents to consider the ease of the petitioners in the light of the decision of ECNEC dated 30-12-2007 and the provisions of SRO No. 182-A in/2005/Shomo/Bidhi-I/S-9/2000 dated 20-6-2005.

<u>9. It appears from the facts and circumstances of the instant case that the petitioners had been given assurances that their services might be transferred/absorbed in the revenue budget. Furthermore, since in similar circumstances the government has implemented the directions of the Supreme Court and absorbed the writ-petitioners in Writ Petition No. 5667 of 2008, it would be discriminatory not to treat the present respondents equally.</u>

10. In the light of the facts and circumstances discussed above, we do not find any illegality or infirmity in the impugned judgment, which calls for any interference. Accordingly, the appeal is dismissed, without however, any order as to costs.

End.
